author: Billy Dukes
title: 8 Canceled Country Celebrities + What They Did To Earn It - NewsBreak
text:
By Billy Dukes ,
9 hours ago Getty Images They say time heals all wounds, but at least one of these canceled country stars would like to argue otherwise.
Words matter. Actions — especially illegal actions — matter. It’s never just about the music, and frankly, that’s a good thing.
When someone is accused of sexual assault and the evidence file is thick, the larger population should pause and consider a punishment not available to a judge.
This list of canceled country stars features three racial slurs, one anti-gay musing and one political statement that by comparison feels minor league to the transgressions around it. Sometimes an artist bounces back. Actually, that’s the truth for five of the eight celebrities listed below.
As for the other three? Well, we’ll see. Maybe we need even more time.
What Does It Mean to Be Canceled? “Canceled” is a term loosely used to describe the loss of significant professional opportunities or status among the general population. It usually begins with a provocative statement or action. Then, public sentiment grows to condemn that statement/action, and by extension, the human being responsible.
Attempts to weaponize cancellation are usually short-lived, especially if the transgression happened years ago. Contrition can go a long way to right wrong-headed statements made as a teenager.
Related : Country Stars Charged With Horrific Crimes — No. 8 Is Infuriating!
Sometimes an act is so heinous that the star just can’t come back, and you’ll find a couple of examples of this on our list of canceled stars.
Amazingly, one superstar did come back after being canceled in another genre. In fact, he’s now in the Country Music Hall of Fame.
This list is an accounting of what happened, with no intended opinion on the outcome. It’s fair to argue that justice was served in some cases and over-served in others, but we won’t be the ones to lead that convo right now.
8 Canceled Country Celebrities + What They Did To Earn It There are certain things you never say and certainly things you never do in country music. Honestly, most of what got these eight celebrities canceled in country would get you scrubbed in other forms of entertainment as well, but not all of them (see No. 4 and No. 7).
This list is here to report history, not to offer an opinion on if justice was served. Five of the eight stars bounced back, and one even worked his way into the Country Music Hall of Fame. Time heals most wounds, it seems. Gallery Credit: Billy Dukes Brett Carlsen, Getty Images Morgan Wallen Morgan Wallen ’s cancellation story is most well-known in 2025. On Jan. 31, 2021, his neighbor’s doorbell camera caught him using the N-word after a night out with friends. TMZ broke the news two days later, and soon after, he’d apologize and try to explain it happened at the end of a long drinking weekend.
That didn’t work, in part because previous transgressions (breaking Saturday Night Live ’s COVID restrictions, getting arrested outside of Kid Rock’s bar) had been followed with similar promises to do better. Radio pulled his music and streamers like Spotify yanked him from playlists. He was also suspended by his record label, and the ACM Awards declared he and his newly released Dangerous: The Double Album would be ineligible for that year’s show.
Fans more than backed him up. Dangerous held the top spot on album charts for much of the year, and within a year, all streaming and airplay entities had removed restrictions. Emma McIntyre, Getty Images Jimmie Allen In May 2023, Jimmie Allen ’s former manager claimed he sexually and verbally abused her and went into great detail during a damning profile in Variety . The unnamed woman described several months of harassment, coercion and rape, and she was not alone.
A month later, a second woman accused Allen of sexual assault and shared that he secretly filmed a sexual encounter in Las Vegas. Allen’s record label first suspended and then dropped him, and several other professional relationships ended.
The former chart-topping country singer has released songs across several genres in the two years since the first accusations, but nothing has gathered as much attention as previous singles released by BBR. Both lawsuits were civil lawsuits, and the first was settled in March 2024.
The second lawsuit ended when a judge awarded a a default judgement in the woman’s favor after Allen and his legal team quit responding to court filings and ignored the judge’s orders. Jerry Markland, Getty Images Phil Robertson Duck Dynasty patriarch Phil Robertson was canceled and then un-canceled before it really mattered.
In late 2013 he told GQ that he thought “homosexual behavior” was sinful. The quote grouped gay people with prostitutes, drunks and terrorists, but he added that he didn’t judge 'em.
“We let God sort 'em out later, you see what I'm saying?” he said.
A&E suspended Robertson, but within two weeks reversed course. The show was never affected. Kevin Winter, Getty Images The Chicks The Chicks were still the Dixie Chicks when singer Natalie Maines ' comments about President Bush got them canceled. On March 10, 2003, she told a London audience she was ashamed the president was from Texas and that was about that for the trio's commercial career.
For context, there was a nationwide debate about President Bush's response to the 9/11 terrorist attacks and growing division among Americans. The country audience was largely in favor of the response, or at least not going to stand for public criticism, especially on foreign soil.
It took about two weeks for nearly every country radio station in America to pull the Chicks' music. Some even went as far as to stage a burning or steamrolling of CDs. They never recovered or apologized, and future records would draw inspiration from reaction to what Maines said. Keystone Via Getty Images Jerry Lee Lewis Jerry Lee Lewis was never canceled in country music. In fact, the opposite is true: country is where he turned when he was canceled by rock and roll.
The "Great Balls of Fire" singer was an A-list celebrity in the late 1950s, but then he married his 13-year-old cousin, Myra. Almost immediately, he went from being paid $10,000 a night to play major venues to playing small bars and clubs. For a decade he was as desired as the flu.
Then — in 1968 — Lewis released a country album and began a 10-year turn as a legit country music hitmaker. It was all good enough to (eventually) get him into the Country Music Hall of Fame, although not everyone was impressed.
Lewis was never even nominated for a CMA Award, and the only attention he got from the ACMs was in instrument categories. Bennett Raglin, Getty Images Dog the Bounty Hunter Duane "Dog" Chapman is one of several country celebrities on this list, and his cancelation will sound familiar to fans of Morgan Wallen.
In October 2007, the National Enquirer got ahold of a recorded phone conversation between Dog and his son, during which he called the son’s girlfriend the N-word. A&E suspended production of Dog the Bounty Hunter, and Chapman would later apologize.
Four months later, A&E production had resumed as they were satisfied with the work Dog had done to make amends. It’d air until 2012, when creative differences separated star from network.
Claims of racism would cost him again in 2021. He was working on a show called Dog Unleashed when (according to Unleashed Entertainment CEO Mike Donovan) the star used racial and homophobic epithets to “attack young African-American kids” starring with Bonnie Chapman in another show called The System . That show would also get canceled. Emma McIntyre, Getty Images Maren Morris Did Maren Morris get canceled or did she just leave? The results are probably the same.
Ever since she took on Jason Aldean (plus his wife) and conservative country music critics, she’s been missing from country music conversations. None of her songs appear among country music’s 500 most played songs of 2025, and that’s more than a little surprising for a singer with three recent No. 1 hits.
It all began when Aldean’s wife Brittany posted something to social media that many perceived to be transphobic. Several people spoke out against what she said, but Morris was the focus of attention, especially after she called Brittany “Insurrection Barbie.”
The parties went back and forth on social media for awhile and about a year later — after the Humble Quest album — Morris said she was leaving country music. Later she’d walk back that comment, but future albums have fallen squarely between genres and have not been nearly as commercially successful. Samuel Corum, Getty Images Paula Deen Paula Deen’s cancelation is the subject of a 2025 documentary she blessed, called Canceled: The Paula Deen Story .
The short version is that in 2013 she was part of a lawsuit brought on by a former restaurant manager who alleged racial discrimination and sexual harassment. During a deposition, Deen admitted she’d used the N-word before, adding that it was a long time ago.
Her justification that — as a Southern woman of age — that’s just how she was raised did her no favors, even as she insisted the word made her skin crawl.
Television networks and sponsors dropped her, and for a couple years she was out there in the wilderness, but eventually she’d return to reality TV by way of Dancing With the Stars and Master Chef . She’d even get back on television and become a popular cookbook author again.
Ahead of the documentary, Deen said the lawsuits stripped her of her soul. See Country Music's 14 Shortest Marriages See country music's shortest marriages, including one that only last four days! Gallery Credit: Billy Dukes Ron Galella, Getty Images Lyle Lovett and Julia Roberts: 639 Days Country singer Lyle Lovett and actor Julia Roberts announced their separation with a simple statement reading (per People ): “We remain close and in great support of each other.” This ended a year-and-a-half-long, closely-watched marriage between the beauty and country music’s rugged Texan.
It was a whirlwind romance if there ever was one. The pair wed just three days after meeting and dove right into busy careers that often left them on opposite ends of the country. After a year, people started to wonder about who each was seen socializing with, and tongues began to wag. But the optimists always believed in love until they made it official. Hulton Archive, Getty Images George Jones and Dorothy Bonvillion: Less Than 1 Year A teenaged George Jones married his first wife Dorothy in a rush in 1950, and she became pregnant just a few months later. In fact, she was six months pregnant when she filed for divorce, citing (per Texas Monthly ) his violent temper and drinking problems. These were the beginning of his wild years, before Jones became a country music legend. The couple did have one child together however, the little-seen Susan, born in 1951. Kevin Winter, Getty Images Carly Pearce and Michael Ray: 282 Days Carly Pearce and Michael Ray dated for 18 months before their October 2019 wedding, and prior to the coronavirus pandemic of 2020, all seemed well, with the "Every Little Thing" singer gushing on her man during a visit with Taste of Country in February. Slowly, they started to disappear from one another's social media pages however, leading to speculation that Pearce felt she had to address during a No. 1 party roundtable for "I Hope You're Happy Now." She filed for divorce on June 19, 2020, per People . Dia Dipasupil, Getty Images Miley Cyrus and Liam Hemsworth: 239 Days Miley Cyrus ' on again, off again romance with Liam Hemsworth officially turned off on Aug. 10, 2019, when he filed for divorce less than eight months after marrying the pop and country singer. Irreconcilable differences was the official reason, but they told People that, "Ever-evolving, changing as partners and individuals, they have decided this is what’s best while they both focus on themselves and careers." Jason Kempin, Getty Images Billy Ray Cyrus and FireRose: 224 Days (Approximately) Billy Ray Cyrus filed for divorce from wife Firerose in late May 2024, after the couple wed on Oct. 10, 2023. TMZ broke the news without much detail. The couple had no children together.
Officially, Cyrus is looking for an annulment with May 22, 2024 listed as the date of separation. The marriage, he says, was obtained by fraud. Still, he's pitching in $5,000 a month for housing until she can get back on her feet. Scott Gries, Getty Images Gary Allan and Danette Day: 190 Days (Approximate) Few recall that Gary Allan dated model Danette Day and even married the pin-up model in late 1998. She was his second wife, and it was short-lived. For reasons never made public, the couple split the following June, although the exact day is not known.
People Kenny Chesney and Renee Zellwegger: 128 Days This one is country music’s most famous short marriages. Kenny Chesney and actor Renee Zellweger met and married in a fever in 2005 and announced a separation just 128 days after their May 9 beachside wedding. She sought an annulment, and later both would admit they were not prepared for marriage. In December that year, the union would be officially dissolved. Believe it or not, we found four marriages that were over quicker than this 4-month-long marriage. Kevin Winter, Getty Images Kid Rock and Pamela Anderson: 122 Days Kid Rock and supermodel and actor Pamela Anderson were the "it" couple for much of the early ‘00s, even though she was fresh off an impulsive marriage to rocker Tommy Lee. They finally married in July 2006, but in November of that year, both filed papers. Actor Sasha Baron Cohen claims it was her role in his movie Borat that put him over the edge, leading to the divorce. Hulton Archive, Getty Images Bobbie Gentry and Bill Harrah: 120 Days The enigmatic Bobbie Gentry married casino magnate Bill Harrah in mid-December 1969, and it was over by mid-April the next year. Very little is known about the couple or the reason for the split (which is on brand for Gentry) , but she did marry twice more, with both of those unions only lasting a couple of years. Jason Davis, Getty Images / Instagram Zac Brown and Kelly Yazdi: 89 Days Zac Brown kept his relationship with Kelly Yazdi very quiet, with news only coming from gossip or celebrity news websites. They were engaged in 2022 and quietly married in Coweta County, Ga. on Aug. 31, 2023. By the end of the year, they'd separated with Zac's team telling TMZ they were in the process of divorcing.
The Zac Brown Band frontman was previously married to Shelly from 2006 to 2018. They have five kids together. Michael Putland, Getty Images Tammy Wynette and Michael Tomlin: 44 Days Tammy Wynette's fourth husband was real estate developer Michael Tomlin, whom she wed on July 18, 1976 after just a few months of dating. By September she'd have the marriage annulled. The Washington Post shared a story reported by Cosmopolitan that he ran along her Florida beachfront firing a gun into the air, but Tomlin denied it.
Her fifth and final husband actually played organ during that ceremony, the paper shares. In fact, George Richey’s then-wife was matron of honor. Technically Wynette's second marriage to Lloyd Amburgey could make this list, as it lasted less than two years, as well. Jason Merritt, Getty Images Jana Kramer and Johnathon Schaech: 12 Days Jana Kramer and actor Johnathon Schaech dated for some time before marrying on July 4, 2010, and while the announcement of their split came 35 days later, US Weekly would later learn that she actually left him after just 12 days. The divorce would be finalized in June 2011. Schaech was actually Kramer’s second husband. Her first was put in prison for abuse and attempted murder, a story she first shared while on Dancing With the Stars in 2016. Harry Langdon, Getty Images Cher and Greg Allman: 9 Days While not a dedicated country star, Greg Allman certainly appeals to country fans, and his marriage to Cher was so wild, we included it. The pair wed just days after her divorce to Sonny Bono was finalized, but nine days later, she filed for divorce. The problem was his drinking and heroin use, but he’d win her back.
And then she'd win him back, he'd win her back again … yeah, they were a rollercoaster for about three years until finally separating for good in 1978. Entertainment Weekly commemorated in a neat and tidy way in 1992. They had one son together, Elijah Blue. Michael Ochs Archive, Getty Images Buck Owens and Jana Jae Greif — About 4 Days The exact number of days that passed between Buck Owens' impulsive, Las Vegas wedding to his fiddle player is not clear but all publications from the time list it as lasting "a few days." Between three and five seems like a good guess. People magazine had the most exploratory look at the couple's romance and the strange, uncomfortable circumstances of their union. Owens makes Porter Wagoner seem downright chivalrous.
In the spring of 1977, Owens was living with the woman who'd eventually become his fourth wife. Jana Rae Greif (who went as just Jana Jae professionally) quit but days later he asked her to marry him. Even though she was aware of his controlling ways she agreed, but the morning after their wedding he told her, (per People ) "I own you lock, stock and barrel."
Surprisingly it was Owens who tried to annul the marriage after just a few days, something made public on the radio before Rae had a chance to hear it for herself. He cited "unsound mind" but didn't specify who he was talking about. There was some back and forth and eventually she cross-filed for annulment. Per Roland Note he filed for divorce in August of 1977, three months after they married. Later he'd say he wasn't drunk on anything but her when he went to the alter.
